# Sparkplug B 3.0 conformance

<!-- Generated by test/tck/coverage.js - do not edit by hand. -->

Which specification requirements this package meets, and where each one is
demonstrated. Requirement ids and text come from the Eclipse Sparkplug TCK's
`Requirements.java`, a transcription of the specification and the only
machine-readable list of it available; the specification document itself is the
authority in any disagreement.

Regenerate after a TCK run:

```bash
test/tck/run-tck-isolated.sh ref/sparkplug   # writes tck-results/
node test/tck/coverage.js ref/sparkplug
```

Results from MQTT 3.1.1, 6 test(s): `PrimaryHostTest` (PASS), `ReceiveCommandTest` (PASS), `SendComplexDataTest` (PASS), `SendDataTest` (PASS), `SessionEstablishmentTest` (PASS but INCOMPLETE), `SessionTerminationTest` (PASS but INCOMPLETE).

Results from MQTT 5.0, 6 test(s): `PrimaryHostTest` (PASS), `ReceiveCommandTest` (PASS), `SendComplexDataTest` (PASS), `SendDataTest` (PASS), `SessionEstablishmentTest` (PASS but INCOMPLETE), `SessionTerminationTest` (PASS but INCOMPLETE).

## Scope

This package implements a Sparkplug **Edge Node**: `mqtt sparkplug device` plus
the `mqtt-sparkplug-broker` configuration node. That is the profile assessed here.

| Profile | Requirements | In scope |
|---|---:|---|
| Edge Node (incl. Monitor) | 203 | Yes - this is what the package is |
| Host Application | 89 | No - see below |
| Broker | 11 | No - this package is not a broker |
| **Defined in total** | **296** | |

## Summary

| | Count |
|---|---:|
| Edge Node requirements exercised by the harness | 178 of 203 |
| — PASS | 177 |
| — MAYBE | 1 |
| Edge Node requirements not exercised | 25 |
| Requirements cited directly in our runtime or specs | 14 |

`MAYBE` is the TCK's outcome for a SHOULD-level requirement, not a failure.
`PASS but INCOMPLETE` on a test means nothing failed and something was never
exercised - see "What counts as a pass" in `README.md`.

## Host Application requirements

**This package ships no Host Application**, so none of the 89 Host profile
requirements is claimed.

`mqtt sparkplug in` subscribes, decodes a Sparkplug payload and emits it as a
Node-RED message - roughly 50 lines that never publish anything. `mqtt sparkplug
out` publishes whatever topic and payload it is handed, with no session semantics
of its own. A Host Application additionally has to publish its STATE birth and
death, track every edge node's session, and originate rebirth and command
messages; none of that exists here.

A flow can of course *act* as a host by combining these nodes with its own logic,
but conformance would then be a property of that flow, not of this package.

| Area | Requirements | Provided |
|---|---:|---|
| operational-behavior | 38 | No - no session or rebirth orchestration |
| host-topic | 15 | No - STATE is never published |
| message-flow | 8 | No - no host session lifecycle |
| payloads-state | 7 | No - STATE is never published |
| payloads-dcmd | 4 | Partly - as above |
| payloads-ncmd | 4 | Partly - as above |
| topics-dcmd | 4 | Partly - as above |
| topics-ncmd | 4 | Partly - `mqtt sparkplug out` can publish an NCMD, but nothing orchestrates it |
| payloads-name | 1 | No |
| components-ph | 1 | No |
| conformance-primary | 1 | No |
| intro-sparkplug | 1 | No |
| principles-birth | 1 | No |

## Where the TCK is wrong

Three assertions read a Sparkplug datatype code as though it were a protobuf field
number. In each the node follows the specification text and the TCK rejects it, so
the fixture works around them rather than bending the node - which would misreport
conformance. Detail in `README.md`.

| Requirement | Issue |
|---|---|
| `payloads-template-instance-members-data` | Text says a DDATA instance MAY carry a subset of members; SendDataTest.checkInstance requires the full set. The fixture updates every member at once. |
| `payloads-propertyset-quality-value-type` | Text mandates type 3 (Int32), which the node emits; the check compares against ValueCase.LONG_VALUE.getNumber(), i.e. 4. The optional Quality key is omitted. |
| `payloads-metric-propertyvalue-type-type` | Property datatypes are filtered through ValueCase.forNumber(), non-null only for 3..10, so String (12) and Boolean (11) properties are rejected. The fixture uses numeric property types. |

## MQTT 5.0

The TCK branches on the version in the CONNECT packet: for each of these pairs it
asserts either the `-311` or the `-50` variant, never both. A run at one version
therefore always leaves the other pair `NOT EXECUTED`.

Both versions were run, so all four are covered - the node connects as 5.0 with
Clean Start set and a Session Expiry Interval of 0, and its intentional
DISCONNECT carries the 'Disconnect with Will Message' reason code.

| Requirement | Status |
|---|---|
| `payloads-ndeath-will-message-publisher-disconnect-mqtt50` | PASS |
| `principles-persistence-clean-session-50` | PASS |
